source.excerpt: It is better to enlighten than merely to shine.
trail: Summa Theologiae II–II, question 188, article 6 compares sharing contemplation with merely contemplating. The checked 1920 English Dominican translation reads “better to enlighten than merely to shine.” This supports the idea but not the displayed English verb. The Summa passage ↗
A second transcription provides the same comparison in question 188. Parallel Summa text ↗

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The passage compares religious lives devoted to contemplation with lives that share its results through teaching and preaching. The light metaphor supports that particular argument; the popular “illuminate” version changes the wording of the inspected English translation.
